results.correct_value: The upper Mowich Face (roughly 1,000-1,300 ft of 55-60 degree snow/ice) is the sustained steep crux; the choss-wall/notch transition on the ridge is a condition-dependent obstacle that can stop parties in dry years, not a fixed crux.
results.evidence: The 1938 first-ascent account describes a 60-degree slope rising about 1,000 ft as the demanding steep ground, and a short rotten-lava traverse on the ridge that needed a rappel. The park climbing rangers' conditions report gives about 1,300 ft of 55-60 degree snow on the upper Mowich Face. A 2025 party was stopped at the knife-edge notch because low snow left a choss wall. The sources agree the notch transition depends on snow cover, and differ on the face's length (1,000 vs 1,300 ft), so the itinerary's categorical 'the crux is' claim is softened and the length stated as a range.
